correctness.rationale: Invertible closed derivative with endpoint-coupled H1 domain and positive regular Sturm–Liouville energy form established directly. Exact transfer determinant verified symbolically; reflected coefficient forces A=D, hence whole eigenvalue characteristic functions identical across complex circles. Ky Fan partial sums are convex in the affine pencil and circularly invariant, giving weak radial submajorization. Schatten Sp norms are strictly convex for 1<p<infinity and Talpha are pairwise distinct, giving strict radial ordering. Direct Hilbert–Schmidt kernel integration yields 2/3 versus 5/6 for a positive nonsymmetric weight at two equal-radius parameters. All claims proven for all dimensions and parameters; finite checks only corroborate.

originality.rationale: The final claim is not the already-known constant-weight spectral formula, explicitly covered by the full 2018 Volterra-pencil proof. The novel focus is the weighted symmetric-class isospectral circles plus all-finite-rank Ky Fan radial ordering and strictly increasing Schatten norms, and an exact smooth asymmetric obstruction. Relevant full texts (2018 pencil, 2010 polynomials, 2013 all-coupled Sturm–Liouville generalities, 2004 Volterra iterates) were compared at theorem/implication level. General boundary determinants supply some methods but neither state nor immediately give the affine weighted-operator majorization statement without the added inverse-domain identification, reflection transfer identity and radial convexity argument. Risks remain from broad inverse-spectral literature and unavailable older weighted singular-value full text.
residual_risks: Fucci–Graham–Kirsten 2013 provides broad coupled Sturm–Liouville spectral machinery, so a weighted corollary could already have appeared elsewhere.
Tuan–Gorenflo 1996 full text not inspected; abstract concerns asymptotic singular values, not parameter-wise finite Ky Fan sums.
Search/index noncoverage does not prove unique originality; the 2018 unweighted theorem has roots for all singular values despite stating only the norm.

value.rationale: Singular-value partial sums control finite-rank approximation and every symmetric gauge. This shows a continuum of heterogeneous, reflection-symmetric Volterra input weights has a phase-blind full singular spectrum and a parameter-majorization hierarchy, while a smooth asymmetric weight fails already for Hilbert–Schmidt norm. The entire rank hierarchy is motivated structurally, unlike a one-off constant or recomputation of the known unweighted norm; no downstream theorem is required.
